instructions: Complete the original TASK-112 implementation from failed_head_sha without widening scope or changing TASK semantics.

RUN-112-001 failed at COMPLETION_GATE because the executor ResultPackage contained unresolved items and produced no candidate delta. Do not clear or suppress a legitimate unresolved condition merely to satisfy the gate; return unresolved as empty only after the TASK-112 implementation, required tests, and evidence are actually complete.

Preserve the audited TASK-112 authority boundary: evidence-complete proposal over existing TASK-109 graph plus canonical TASK-111 POSITIVE_CONNECTED group, explicit Human APPROVE/REJECT only, no pairwise re-execution, no conflict override, no canonical family/product/variant IDs, no actual merge, no persistence/catalog mutation, and no executor push/merge/publication.

acceptance.condition: An immutable platform-neutral FamilyMergeProposal can be created only from one existing MultiObservationResolutionGraph plus one exact canonical TASK-111 POSITIVE_CONNECTED group from that graph, without accepting source packs or invoking TASK-108/TASK-109 entity-resolution execution again.

Proposal creation fails closed for SINGLETON, CONFLICTED, forged, stale, absent, duplicated, or otherwise non-canonical group inputs before producing an approvable proposal; TASK-109 conflicts are never repaired, suppressed, or Human-overridden by this boundary.

A proposal preserves the exact canonical TASK-111 member tuple and exposes exactly N*(N-1)/2 induced pair evidence values, with one and only one value for every unordered member pair and no omitted or duplicated pair.

Every proposal pair evidence value preserves the exact TASK-108 relationship, confidence, reasons, and ResolutionEvidence from the corresponding TASK-109 result, including direct UNCERTAIN pairs; no pairwise semantic value is recomputed, aggregated, upgraded, downgraded, or rewritten.

Pair endpoints and the complete pair sequence are canonically presented from TASK-111 member order, so reversing/permuting equivalent source observation input before TASK-109 evaluation produces semantically identical merge proposals despite raw TASK-108 left/right caller orientation.

An immutable Human decision record can be created only from an exact FamilyMergeProposal plus explicit APPROVE or REJECT, explicit non-empty single-line actor, and explicit timezone-aware decided_at; invalid/missing decision data fails before any result is returned and no wall-clock default is used.

Positive connectivity, confidence, relationship values, reasons, evidence, member count, or proposal construction never auto-create APPROVE. A proposal containing one or more UNCERTAIN pairs remains approvable only through an explicit Human APPROVE decision.

APPROVE authorizes only future canonical product-family identity creation for the exact proposal member set and does not rewrite pairwise relationships, infer transitive truth, assert exact-variant equivalence, merge observations, assign IDs, or mutate a catalog; REJECT likewise records only the decision.

The public TASK-112 API exposes no proposal/group/family/product/variant ID, aggregate or merge confidence, automated merge recommendation, persistence, queueing, filesystem write, network/browser/Drive/LLM/scoring/ranking/ ingestion/catalog mutation, or external-service side effect.

Focused deterministic regression tests cover an approvable positive-connected group containing an internal UNCERTAIN pair, complete N*(N-1)/2 pair matrix, exact evidence preservation, canonical pair orientation/order across input permutations, singleton rejection, conflicted-group rejection, forged/stale group rejection, malformed/missing/duplicate induced-pair failure, explicit APPROVE/REJECT, actor/timestamp validation, immutability, zero entity-resolution re-execution, and zero side effects.

assumptions: MultiObservationResolutionGraph from TASK-109 remains the canonical bounded evidence container and preserves every unordered pairwise EntityResolutionResult plus any ProductFamilyConsistencyConflict diagnostics.
ProvisionalProductFamilyGroup and group_resolution_graph from TASK-111 remain the sole provisional-grouping authority; TASK-112 must not recreate grouping semantics independently.

TASK-108 remains the sole semantic authority for pairwise relationship, confidence, reasons, and ResolutionEvidence values. TASK-112 may canonicalize presentation orientation/order only; it must not recompute or reinterpret those values.

A POSITIVE_CONNECTED TASK-111 group can legitimately contain direct UNCERTAIN pairs. UNCERTAIN remains unresolved evidence and must remain visible to the Human rather than being upgraded, suppressed, or treated as a negative edge.
A TASK-111 CONFLICTED group already contains TASK-109 contradictory evidence and is not approvable in this milestone. Conflict adjudication/repair remains separate later work.
Explicit Human decision fields should follow the proven TASK-096 pattern: APPROVE/REJECT only, a non-empty actor identifier, and an explicit timezone-aware decided_at with no wall-clock default.
Canonical product-family IDs, sellable variant IDs, catalog persistence, evidence aggregation, retrieval, RAG, and autonomous merge policy remain later M3 work.

hard: The proposal operation must consume one existing MultiObservationResolutionGraph and one ProvisionalProductFamilyGroup and must never accept ProductSourcePack values as an alternate path.

The supplied group must match exactly one canonical group produced by the existing TASK-111 group_resolution_graph(graph) projection for the same graph; forged, stale, absent, duplicated, or non-canonical group values must fail closed before a proposal is returned.

Only a canonical TASK-111 group whose status is POSITIVE_CONNECTED and whose conflict tuple is empty may become a FamilyMergeProposal. SINGLETON and CONFLICTED groups must fail closed and cannot be Human-approved in TASK-112.

Proposal creation must never call resolve_product_entities, resolve_multi_observations, MultiObservationEntityResolver.resolve, or any equivalent TASK-108/TASK-109 re-execution authority. Calling the existing deterministic TASK-111 grouping projection solely to validate exact group lineage is permitted and must not recreate grouping semantics independently.

For a proposal containing N members, the proposal must expose exactly N*(N-1)/2 pair evidence values: one and only one for every unordered pair of proposal members, with no pair omitted or duplicated.

Each proposal pair evidence value must preserve exactly the corresponding TASK-108 relationship, confidence, reasons, and ResolutionEvidence values from the TASK-109 graph. TASK-112 may only canonicalize left/right presentation and outer pair ordering.

UNCERTAIN pairwise evidence inside an otherwise POSITIVE_CONNECTED group must remain explicit in the proposal and must not block proposal creation by itself. It may proceed past this boundary only through an explicit Human APPROVE.

Pair endpoints must be oriented according to the canonical TASK-111 member ordering and the complete pair sequence must be deterministically ordered by those member positions, so equivalent graph/input permutations yield semantically identical FamilyMergeProposal values even though TASK-108 raw left/right bindings follow caller order.

Proposal creation must fail closed if the graph does not contain exactly one preserved pairwise result for every unordered pair of the canonical group members or if any pairwise result references a malformed/non-member endpoint for the induced proposal evidence.
FamilyMergeProposal, its pair evidence values, and the Human decision record must be immutable.

The Human decision contract must support exactly explicit APPROVE and REJECT decisions and require an explicit non-empty single-line actor identifier plus an explicit timezone-aware decided_at datetime; wall-clock defaults and implicit actor values are forbidden.

No proposal status, positive connectivity, pairwise relationship, confidence, reason, evidence code, member count, or other machine-derived value may automatically create or imply an APPROVE decision.

An APPROVE decision means only that the Human authorizes a later milestone to treat the exact proposal member set as one canonical product family. It must not rewrite any preserved pairwise relationship, assert exact-variant equivalence, create canonical identity, or perform any merge/catalog mutation.
A REJECT decision records only the explicit Human decision and must not mutate, split, repair, or rewrite the proposal, graph, group, or any external state.
TASK-112 must expose no proposal_id, group_id, family_id, product_id, variant_id, merge_confidence, aggregate confidence, automatic merge flag, or persistent catalog authority.

TASK-112 must be deterministic and side-effect-free for the same graph/group and explicit Human inputs, with zero filesystem mutation, persistence, database, queue, network, browser, Drive, LLM, scoring, ranking, ingestion, catalog-write, or external-service side effects.
Do not push from executor execution.

task.problem: TASK-111 can now organize an existing TASK-109 resolution graph into provisional positive-connected groups, but positive connectivity is not transitive product truth: a valid group may still contain direct UNCERTAIN pairwise relationships. Letting a Human approve only a member list would hide material uncertainty and could accidentally promote graph connectivity into authoritative same-family evidence. Conversely, requiring every pair to be positive would make Human approval redundant and prevent an explicit Human from adjudicating a bounded evidence-complete proposal. TASK-112 must therefore bind each approvable group back to the exact preserved TASK-109 pairwise evidence for every unordered member pair, present that evidence canonically and permutation-invariantly, reject singleton/conflicted groups, and record only an explicit Human decision. The decision may authorize later canonical-family creation for that exact member set, but TASK-112 itself must not merge observations, rewrite relationships, assign IDs, persist a catalog, or infer missing pairwise truth.
